content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed comprehensive guidelines on systematic screening for tuberculosis (TB) disease, which are detailed in Module 2 of their consolidated guidelines. These guidelines were created following a rigorous methodology, involving input from three expert groups: the Guideline Steering Group (composed of WHO staff), the Guideline Development Group (GDG, including external experts, national TB program managers, academics, researchers, and patient representatives), and the External Review Group (ERG, consisting of peer reviewers). The process began with the preparation of a background document and the drafting of PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome) questions to guide the update. These were reviewed and approved by the WHO Guideline Review Committee. Evidence reviews were commissioned, and outcomes of interest were scored by GDG members on a scale of 1 to 9 to prioritize their importance. Most outcomes were deemed critical for decision-making. For diagnostic accuracy questions, outcomes such as sensitivity and specificity were pre-specified and not scored. The GDG held virtual meetings, including 13 webinars between June and October 2020, to discuss the evidence and reach consensus on recommendations. A quorum of 50% of GDG members was required for meetings to proceed, and at least 80% agreement was needed to approve recommendations if consensus was not unanimous. Evidence was summarized using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) approach, which assessed the quality of evidence and guided discussions on benefits, harms, costs, feasibility, and equity. Recommendations were categorized as either strong or conditional based on the confidence in the evidence and the balance of desirable versus undesirable effects. The guidelines were reviewed and endorsed by all GDG members, with input from the ERG incorporated into the final version. Final approval was granted by the Guideline Review Committee on March 5, 2021. The guidelines are freely available on the WHO website and will be widely disseminated through conferences, meetings, and the WHO eTB guidelines platform. An operational handbook will accompany the guidelines to support implementation, and WHO will assist national programs in planning and executing systematic TB screening interventions. The GDG and ERG members completed declarations of interest, which were evaluated to identify potential conflicts. Intellectual conflicts were not considered grounds for exclusion, as expertise was deemed essential. Some members declared interests that were judged not to conflict with the guidelines' objectives, while one member was recused from discussions on a specific topic due to a potential conflict. The guidelines emphasize the importance of creating a supportive policy environment, allocating resources, and training healthcare staff to implement systematic TB screening effectively. National programs are encouraged to engage affected populations, communities, and relevant stakeholders in planning and implementation. The uptake and impact of the guidelines will be monitored through WHO's Global TB Data Monitoring system, and updates will be made as new evidence becomes available.
